subject: Polity
description: Multi-member ECI, conduct of elections, registration of parties, recognition, model code

questions.stem: The Election Commission of India became a multi-member body permanently from:
questions.explanation: ECI — single-member body (CEC alone) from 1950 to 1989. Briefly became 3-member in 1989 (Dinesh Goswami's reforms), reverted to single in 1990, and made permanently 3-member from 1 October 1993 — during T.N. Seshan's tenure. Currently 1 CEC + 2 ECs. CEC and ECs have equal say; majority decision rules. CEC removable only by impeachment (Articles 324(5), same as SC judge). ECs removable on CEC's recommendation.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: T.N. Seshan, who as CEC (1990-96) brought sweeping electoral reforms, was the:
questions.explanation: T.N. Seshan — 10th CEC (December 1990 – December 1996). Reforms: enforcement of Model Code of Conduct, voter ID cards (EPIC), action against booth capturing, enforcement of expenditure limits, mandatory affidavits. First CEC — Sukumar Sen (1950-58). Other notable CECs — N. Gopalaswami (Sept 2008-July 2009), S.Y. Quraishi, V.S. Sampath, Sunil Arora, Sushil Chandra. The Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act 2023 changed the appointment panel.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Recognition of a political party as a 'NATIONAL party' by ECI requires the party to fulfill ANY ONE of the following — which is INCORRECT?

options.option_text: Has 2% LS seats from at least 3 states
Recognised as state party in at least 4 states
Has at least 200 MPs across LS + RS
Has secured 6% valid votes in 4 states + 4 LS seats

questions.explanation: ECI conditions for NATIONAL party (any one): (1) 6% valid votes in any 4 states + ≥4 LS seats; (2) 2% LS seats from at least 3 different states (current requirement = 11 LS seats from 3 states); (3) recognised as state party in at least 4 states. There is NO 200-MP threshold. Currently ~6 national parties: BJP, Congress, BSP, NPP, AAP, CPI-M (varies as ECI reviews periodically). 'State party' has separate criteria. Reserved election symbols are tied to recognition.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The CEC and Election Commissioners are appointed (post-2023 Act) by:

options.option_text: President on recommendation of a 3-member committee — PM, LoP/Single-largest-opposition leader in LS, and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by PM

questions.explanation: Pre-2023 — President appointed CEC/ECs on Government's advice (essentially executive choice). The Anoop Baranwal v UoI (March 2023) Supreme Court bench ordered a CJI-PM-LoP panel to advise. Parliament passed CEC and Other ECs (Appointment) Act 2023 in December 2023 — 3-member panel: PM (chair) + LoP-LS + Union Minister nominated by PM. Replaces the SC's CJI-inclusion. The change was contested in court.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Tenure of the CEC / EC is:

options.option_text: 5 years or until 70 years of age
6 years or up to age 65, whichever is earlier

questions.explanation: CEC and ECs hold office for 6 years OR till they attain 65 years, whichever comes first. Salary equivalent to a Supreme Court judge. CEC's salary cannot be reduced after appointment (security similar to SC judge). On retirement, CEC/ECs are not eligible for further employment under State or Central government. Resignation accepted by President.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Election expenditure limit per Lok Sabha candidate (most large states, 2024) is:
questions.explanation: ECI raised LS candidate spending limit to ₹95 lakh in big states (Jan 2022, last revised under Election Conduct Rules 1961). Smaller states/UTs — ₹75 lakh. State Assembly large states — ₹40 lakh; smaller — ₹28 lakh. Limit is on candidate spending, NOT party expenditure (which is separately tracked). Candidate must file expense statement within 30 days of declaration of result. Exceeding the limit can lead to disqualification under Section 10A of RPA 1951. Critics say true spending is far higher, often via 'paid news' and informal channels.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: VVPAT (Voter-Verified Paper Audit Trail) was introduced by ECI to:

options.option_text: Replace EVMs entirely with paper ballots
Provide paper trail allowing voter to verify their vote was recorded correctly

questions.explanation: VVPAT — printer attached to EVM Ballot Unit. After voter casts vote, a paper slip with candidate's name + symbol + serial number is printed, displayed for 7 seconds in a sealed window, then drops into a sealed compartment. Allows voter to verify but voter doesn't take the slip home. Recount possible if EVM result is challenged. SC (Subramanian Swamy v ECI 2013) directed VVPAT introduction. First used in by-elections from Sep 2013; full rollout by 2019 LS election. Random match of 5 EVMs per assembly mandated.
